neighbours.label: 'to' after a coercive causative: 'forcing them to', 'compelled him to' (permission and invitation are near misses)
fire: The drought drove the deer away, forcing them to search higher up for grass.
The new rule forces landlords to repair old boilers.
Hunger compelled the soldiers to surrender the fort.
The flood forced the villagers to abandon their homes.
High fees are forcing students to drop out of college.
The strike obliged the airline to cancel its flights.
Rising water forced him to climb onto the roof.
The blockade forced the city to ration its bread.
quiet: The drought brought the deer down, letting them search lower down for grass.
The new rule lets landlords repair old boilers.
Hunger led the soldiers past the walls of the fort.
The flood reached the villagers and their homes.
Low fees are helping students to stay on at college.
The strike encouraged the airline to review its flights.
Rising water invited him to swim near the roof.
The blockade allowed the city to save its bread.

notes: Card: mixed peaks (' to' 4 of the top 32). Probes: 'forcing them to' 0.87; 'more costly to' 0.22, 'gives up' 0.24, 'lets them walk ... to' 0.01. The label is one context; the pole's other peaks (' loss', ' up', ' find') are not covered.
